note: Legs follow the week-10 gate in research/kimi_rounds/round2_kimi.md and the sizing in research/humanoid_legs.md. The 3D model is Stanford's ToddlerBot (MIT), the closest open design to our servo walker. 'links' are ToddlerBot URDF link-name prefixes.

stages.title: Learn to walk in simulation
stages.text: Train a walking policy for this exact robot in MuJoCo, starting from the ToddlerBot and Open Duck code. No hardware needed yet.

stages.title: Build the real walker
stages.text: If the torso build is on schedule and at least C$400 is left: a 0.62 m biped, 12 leg joints, about C$390, sharing the torso's computer and cameras.

stages.title: Full-size legs
stages.text: Legs strong enough to carry the life-size torso need brushless actuators, around C$150-250 per joint times 12. That's the next budget.

parts.name: Hips
parts.actuator: Hip pitch: STS3250 (50 kg·cm). Hip roll + yaw: STS3215 (30 kg·cm).
parts.made: Printed PETG pelvis and hip brackets

parts.name: Knees
parts.actuator: STS3250 (the knee does the most work when walking)

parts.name: Ankles + feet
parts.actuator: Ankle pitch: STS3250. Ankle roll: STS3215.
parts.made: Printed feet with TPU soles for grip

parts.name: Body + balance
parts.actuator: BNO085 IMU for balance, 3S LiPo battery, Waveshare bus adapter
parts.made: Printed torso; shares the main robot's computer and cameras
